wordingCorrection.before: `JiraWorkflowStage` never-guess proven: fuzzed/unrecognized workflow-status names always resolve to `blocked`, never `done`.
wordingCorrection.after: `JiraWorkflowStage` never-guess proven: a fuzzed/unrecognized workflow-status NAME never resolves to `done` on the name alone — with no category hint it always resolves to `blocked`, and with a `new`/`indeterminate` hint it resolves to `planned`/`in_progress`. There is exactly one case in which an unrecognized name resolves to `done`: when Jira's own `statusCategory.key` is `done`. That is deliberate and is the safer direction, not the weaker one — `statusCategory.key` is a fixed, Jira-computed three-value enum chosen by a workflow admin, not attacker-shaped free text, and criterion 7's closing-transition gate depends on it: a real closing transition to a site-custom status name ("Ready for Prod") must still be recognized as closing, or it would bypass the done-evidence gate while closing the issue for real. The correction matches roadmap/18 §In scope's own phrasing of the rule — "an unrecognized remote status always resolves to `blocked`, never SILENTLY to `done`" — which the exit criterion restates without the word "silently".

criteria.notes: Why this is a precision correction and not a lost guarantee, stated plainly because the protocol forbids the latter. Implementing the criterion's literal words would make the system LESS safe, not more: `mapJiraStatusToWorkflowStage` feeds `issues.planTransition`'s done-ness resolution, so mapping a Jira-classified `done` status with a site-custom NAME to `blocked` would drop both the `closing transitions` capability flag and `assertDoneTransitionHasEvidence`, while the POST still closed the issue. The guarantee the box actually carries — this connector never invents `done` out of a name it does not recognize — is fully proven above, at both the mapper and the connector level. The phase file's own §In scope sentence carries the word "silently"; the exit criterion drops it. The check was not changed to fit the words, and the words in the phase file are preserved verbatim with the correction appended as a dated annotation.
